speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant experiencing recurrent stridor and wheezing, particularly during certain activities. To help me understand your condition, please tell me: when do these breathing difficulties typically occur?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with possible associated Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD).

The symptoms of stridor worsening with neck flexion, crying, and feeding, combined with post-prandial vomiting, are classic for this condition. I will monitor you closely for signs of airway obstruction or failure to thrive.
